Tate's marmoset, Marmosa paraguayana, is a small didelphid marsupial that exhibits a remarkable set of life-history traits typical of the family, including a very small neonatal mass. Newborn pups weigh just 0.1 grams [Wwb = 0.1 grams], a value consistent with the extremely altricial state of neonates across the Didelphidae. Females of this species attain a maximum adult body mass of 170 grams [Wwi = 170 grams], which positions them as moderate-sized members of their genus.
